claim: daojia/daojiao 两范畴：daojia 为汉初目录学范畴（'哲学'文本），daojiao 指东汉末起自称 daojiao 的宗教运动；历史上道徒对此二分不感兴趣。
locator: IEP "Daoist Philosophy" §1：'Daoism corresponds to both Daojia ("Dao family" or "school of the Dao"), an early Han dynasty (c. 100s B.C.E.) term which describes so-called "philosophical" texts and thinkers such as Laozi and Zhuangzi, and Daojiao ("teaching of the Dao"), which describes various so-called "religious" movements dating from the late Han dynasty (c. 100s C.E.) onward.'；'While modern scholars, especially those in the West, have been preoccupied with classifying Daoist material as either "philosophical" or "religious," historically Daoists themselves have been uninterested in such categories and dichotomies.'
note: 本条为全包边界立论的第一支点。

claim: 诸宗教运动自认 daojiao，起点是142年张道陵受神化老君降授的传说（传记性来源）。
locator: IEP：'all self-identified as daojiao ("teaching of the dao"), beginning with the reception of revelations from the deified Laozi by the Celestial Masters (Tianshi) lineage founder, Zhang Daoling, in 142 C.E.'；'According to an account in Ge Hong's Biographies of Spirit Immortals, Laozi appeared to Zhang (c. 142 CE) and gave him a commission'
note: 传说性来源已如实标注（出自《神仙传》系）。
uncertainty: 142年为传统系年，事件带传说性质。

claim: SEP 现行条目把 Daoism 整体处理为自然实践哲学、通篇不涉教团史；道家/道教二名皆造于汉代；王弼编定《老子》通行本、郭象编定《庄子》。
locator: SEP "Daoism"（访问所见 2025-04-19 修订版）：'Chinese Daoism is a Chinese philosophy of natural practice structured around a normative focus on dào (道 path, way).'；'The terms for the Daoist school (道家 dàojiā) and its teachings (道教 dàojiào) were both coined during the eclectic Han dynasty following the Qin (221–206 BC) repression.'；'Wang Bi (226-249) curated the received Laozi (Daode Jing). Guo Xiang later did the same with the Zhuangzi.'
note: 该条目实测无 Celestial Masters/Shangqing/Lingbao/alchemy 等词（grep 0 命中），是'只写哲学面'的直接证据。
uncertainty: 仅对 2025-04-19 访问版本有效；历史修订未核读。

claim: 庄子（late 4th century BC）为古典哲学道家枢纽人物，《庄子》为汇编；其自然主义与《老子》主题塑造禅宗；'休谟'式刻画。
locator: SEP "Zhuangzi"（2024-03-24 修订版）：'Zhuangzi (Chuang-tzu 莊子 "Master Zhuang" late 4th century BC) is the pivotal figure in Classical Philosophical Daoism. The Zhuangzi is a compilation of his and others' writings'；'Six centuries later, elements of Zhuangzi's naturalism, along with themes found in the text attributed to Laozi helped shape Chan Buddhism (Japanese Zen)'；'Zhuangzi strikes us as more the Hume of his tradition than a system builder'

claim: 《想尔注》把道神格化为太上老君、以道诫重构修行；残卷性质与仅存3—37章注。
locator: 维基文库《老子想爾注》逐字：'一者，道也。……一散形為氣，聚形為太上老君，常治崑崙。或言虛無，或言自然，或言無名，皆同一耳。今布道誡，教人守誡不違，即為守一矣。不行其誡，即為失一也.'（頁頭：'（原書為殘卷，由此句起，上缺）'，署名'作者：張道陵 東漢'）；Wikipedia Xiang'er：'the Xiang'er that survives only comments upon 3d through 37th chapters of the Daodejing'；'was discovered in the Buddhist Mogao caves at Dunhuang'
note: S15 为一手文本、S4 为背景定位，两源互补。
uncertainty: 署名张道陵为传统署名；作者四说见 S14。

claim: 《想尔注》系年190—220、'早期资料称作者为张鲁'；immortality 非《道德经》本身的重要话题。
locator: Wikipedia Xiang'er：'The Xiang'er was likely written between 190 and 220 CE, a time when the Celestial Masters controlled a theocratic state in Sichuan.'；'Early sources indicate that the text was written by Zhang Lu, the third Celestial Master and grandson to Zhang Daoling'；'importantly, immortality is not a significant topic in the Daodejing itself'
note: 'immortality is not...'一句是'宗教化改写'论证的直接支撑。

claim: 《想尔注》作者与年代未有定论（张陵/张鲁/六朝初年/南北朝诸说）；唐末佚失、今存北朝人所书敦煌残卷；神道设教把道拟人化；饶宗颐校刊本与柏夷英译本行世。
locator: 中文维基百科'老子想爾註'：'有關其作者與年代未有定論，有成書於張陵、張魯、六朝初年、南北朝初年等多種說法'；'大約於唐末動亂時佚失，今僅存一北朝人所寫的殘本在世，發現於敦煌石窟中'；'《想爾注》神道設教，把「道」擬人化'；'《想爾注》今有饒宗頤的校刊本及柏夷（Stephen R. Bokenkamp）的英譯本行世'

claim: 葛洪以'玄'为本体：'玄者，自然之始祖，而萬殊之大宗也'。
locator: 维基文库《抱朴子/卷01》〈暢玄〉逐字：'玄者，自然之始祖，而萬殊之大宗也。眇眛乎其深也，故稱微焉。綿邈乎其遠也，故稱妙焉.'；'胞胎元一，範鑄兩儀'；'故玄之所在，其樂不窮。玄之所去，器弊神逝.'

claim: '我命在我不在天'出自《黄白》引《龟甲文》；'长生可学得'同篇。
locator: 维基文库《抱朴子/卷16》〈黃白〉逐字：'龜甲文曰：我命在我不在天，還丹成金億萬年。古人豈欺我哉？'；'又曰，金銀可自作，自然之性也，長生可學得者也.'

claim: 重玄学派为唐代传统、哲学受佛教中观影响、成玄英（fl. 631–655）为关键人物、以《老子》《庄子》义疏知名。
locator: Wikipedia Taoist philosophy：'Another influential Daoist tradition from the Tang dynasty is the Twofold Mystery School (Chinese: 重玄, pinyin: Chóngxuán). Their philosophy was influenced by Buddhist Madhyamaka thought. A key thinker from this tradition was Cheng Xuanying (成玄英, fl. 631–655), who is known for his influential commentaries on the Daodejing and Zhuangzi.'

claim: 成玄英生平：约7世纪初生；631年诏入长安任西华观观主；636/638佛道论辩；647年参与《道德经》梵译（主bodhi被改定mārga）并请译《河上公注》未果；同年检《三皇经》；约653流放；685—690年间卒；《庄子疏》合郭象注为《南华真经注疏》三十卷。
locator: Wikipedia Cheng Xuanying：'Cheng Xuanying was born sometime around the first decade of the seventh century, in Shan Prefecture in modern-day Henan. He lived in Donghai in seclusion until 631, when he was summoned to the Tang capital Chang'an and appointed the head monk of Xihua Abbey by the imperial decree of Emperor Taizong.'；'In 636 and 638 Cheng was present for a series of debates between Daoists and Buddhists ... along with Cai Zihuang (蔡子晃), a fellow Chongxuan adherent.'；'Cheng, again along with Cai, participated in the translation of the Daodejing into Sanskrit in 647, headed by the eminent Buddhist monk Xuanzang. ... Xuanying wanted to translate the term Dao as bodhi, but Xuanzang rejected it in favour of mārga'；'He also requested that the Heshanggong commentary be translated as well, which Xuanzang similarly denied.'；'He died sometime between 685 and 690.'；'Cheng wrote one of the more significant commentaries to the Zhuangzi, the Subcommentary to the Zhuangzi (莊子疏). His commentary ... is a sub-commentary to Guo Xiang's; traditionally, both commentaries have been handed down together. ... (Nánhúa Zhēnjīng Zhùshū 南華真經注疏) in 30 juan'
uncertainty: '师事刘进喜'为'一些学者'之说（'Some scholars alternatively maintain...'），packet 未采为主张。

claim: 内丹定义与历史：内外丹'据称唐代分离'；《参同契》最早理论炼丹书（传魏伯阳142年作，他处标 doubtful）；现存内丹文献始于8世纪上半叶；neidan 一词宋初流行；自称'金丹之道'。
locator: Wikipedia Neidan：'Neidan, or internal alchemy ..., is an array of esoteric doctrines and physical, mental, and spiritual practices that Taoist initiates use in hopes to prolong life and create an immortal spiritual body that would survive after death.'；'Neidan is part of the Chinese alchemical meditative tradition that is said to have been separated into internal and external (Waidan) at some point during the Tang dynasty. The Cantong qi (The Kinship of the Three) is the earliest known book on theoretical alchemy in China; it was written by the alchemist Wei Boyang in 142 AD. This text influenced the formation of neidan, whose earliest existing texts date from the first half of the 8th century.'；'Liu Xiyue's 988 ... has the earliest datable mention of the terms neidan and waidan.'；'The authors of several neidan articles refer to their teachings as the Way of the Golden Elixir (jindan zhi dao).'
note: 同条目另有 'mentioned above is doubtful' 句指魏伯阳署名/年代疑点，已入 evidenceLimits 与 works。

claim: 《悟真篇》1075年内丹经典；张伯端987?—1082（生年三说）、三教学者、1069年'据称'成都遇师。
locator: Wikipedia Wuzhen pian：'Wuzhen pian ... is a 1075 Taoist classic on Neidan-style internal alchemy. Its author Zhang Boduan (張伯端; 987?–1082) was a Song dynasty scholar of the Three teachings (Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhism).'；'in 1069 he allegedly experienced sudden realization from a Taoist master who instructed him in Neidan internal alchemy.'

claim: 王重阳三教一所立教、全真以内丹为重心（修性调命）、引入佛教式出家建制；全真与正一道并为两大教派、1170年起于山东。
locator: Wikipedia Taoist philosophy：'a scholar ... who taught that the "three teachings" (Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism), "when investigated, prove to be but one school". The Quanzhen school was syncretic, combining elements from Buddhism (such as monasticism) and Confucianism with past Taoist traditions. Neidan, a form of internal alchemy, became a major emphasis of the Quanzhen sect. Wang Chongyang taught that "immortality of the soul" (shén-xiān, 神仙) can be attained within this life by entering seclusion, cultivating one's "internal nature" (xìng, 性), and harmonizing them with one's "personal fate" (mìng-yùn, 命運).'"；Wikipedia Quanzhen School：'The Quanzhen School (全真 ...) is currently one of the two dominant denominations of Daoism in China (the other being Zhengyi Dao or "Orthodox Unity"). It originated in the Shandong peninsula in 1170. One of its founders was master Wang Chongyang (1113–1170).'"；IEP：'Into this confusion came Wang Zhe (1113-1170 CE), the founder of Quanzhen (Complete Perfection) Daoism. It was Wang's goal to bring the three teachings into a single great synthesis. For the first time, Daoist teachers adopted monastic forms of life'

claim: 上清派起于杨羲茅山降经（360—370），把葛洪式外丹技术转为反思式冥想，为内丹传统之始；灵宝经为葛巢甫所造、大量借自佛教。
locator: IEP §12：'Yang Xi was the most prominent medium recipient of the Maoshan revelations (360-370 CE). These revelations came from spirits who were local heroes named the Mao brothers ... Yang Xi's writings formed the basis for Highest Purity (Shangqing) Daoism.'；'The importance of these texts philosophically speaking is to be found in their idealization of the quest for immortality and transference of the material practices of the alchemical science of Ge Hong into a form of reflective meditation. In fact, the Shangqing school of Daoism is the beginning of the tradition known as "inner alchemy" (neidan)'; 'a descendent of Ge Hong, named Ge Chaofu went into a mediumistic trance and authored a set of texts called the Numinous Treasure (Lingbao) teachings. These works were ritual recitation texts similar to Buddhist sutras, and indeed they borrowed heavily from Buddhism.'
note: 中文写法'葛巢甫'从 S20（中文维基，无来源模板条目，仅用于名形核对）；S2 页面拼写为 Ge Chaofu。
uncertainty: 中文写法'葛巢甫'与 S2 拼写 Ge Chaofu 对应，未见中文字形来源，packet 已在 detail 中以拼写呈现。

claim: 陆修静（406—477）整合诸源流成'道教'（Dàojiào）共同信仰文本实践；寇谦之（365—448）改革天师道立新诫律。
